abstract: We describe the implementation of the SMPTE ST 2110 suite of standards in the construction of a new television broadcast facility for two stations in the Washington, D.C., market. We discuss problems encountered during this project, which ran between 2019 and 2021, along with their solutions and lessons learned. Particular emphasis is placed on difficulties caused by the limited adoption of Networked Media Open Specification (NMOS) IS-04 and IS-05 by manufacturers in their ST 2110 devices.

authors.bio: Jim Beahn is the vice president of engineering and operations at WTTG/WDCA Fox Television Stations, Bethesda, MD. He has spent the last 35 years working in broadcast engineering and information technology for several of the local television stations in Washington, D.C.
authors.name: Jim Beahn

authors.bio: Nik Kumar is a broadcast systems engineering professional who has successfully managed and led project engineering and integration teams in completing system integration projects for a wide range of customers in the broadcast/media and entertainment industry for over 15 years. Kumar is currently a solutions architect with Diversified, Kenilworth, NJ, and has recently led the Diversified project engineering team in successfully launching WTTG–Fox5 D.C.,’s on-air production from a brand-new facility in Bethesda, MD. WTTG is Fox TV Group’s first full SMPTE ST 2110 implementation in the country. Kumar received a BS degree in electrical engineering as well as a master’s degree in engineering management.
authors.name: Nikhilesh Kumar
